title: Document Search
description_html:
You are given two inputs:

  1. A document consisting of multiple English sentences. The character set is unrestricted and may include letters, numbers, punctuation, and other characters.
  2. A targets list, where each element is a single word.

Your tasks are:

  • Determine whether all target words appear in the document (respecting multiplicity in the target list).
  • Count the number of occurrences of each target word in the document.
  • Find the shortest contiguous sub-document that contains all target words at least the number of times they appear in the target list.

The sub-document must be a continuous portion of the original document (so punctuation and spacing are preserved in the output).

Example

document = "This is an example document. This document isn't very special."
targets  = ['document', 'document', 'isnt']

match   = True
count   = { 'document': 2, 'isnt': 1 }
subDoc  = "document. This document isn't"

Note: "isnt" is treated the same as "isn't" (strip non-alphanumeric for matching).

Approach hint

  1. Tokenize the document into normalized words (lowercase + strip non-[a-z0-9]); keep each token's (start, end) char offsets in the original document so we can slice it back at the end.
  2. Build a multi-set of targets — e.g. Counter(['document', 'document', 'isnt']) = {document:2, isnt:1}.
  3. Sliding window over the token stream. Expand right until the window covers all target counts (track matched count); then contract from the left while it still covers. Record the shortest window's (l_token, r_token).
  4. Slice the original document by the char offsets tokens[l_token].start … tokens[r_token].end to return subDoc with original punctuation intact.

This is the classic Minimum Window Substring pattern lifted from characters to tokenized words. Closest LC: LC 76 (direct algorithmic match); siblings: LC 30 (Substring with Concatenation of All Words — word-based), LC 819 (tokenize + punctuation strip), LC 209 (sliding-window template warm-up).
